payload.claim: The fourth acceptance criterion states the suite witness's `CellSpec` and `intake.Spec` calls 'each yield exactly six new integrity failures,' enumerating only the deleted spec's id, the two nested-directory ids, the outside id, the renamed file's name-prefix id, and the `.txt` file's id. The shipped witness instead asserts `len(cited) == 7` and folds a seventh id, `SA-0050` (declared by `.saffron/specs/done/README.md`'s own `id:` line, written at base and cited via `# readme SA-0050` in the head commit's `notes.py`), into the failing set. `README.md` is never named as passing or failing anywhere in the criterion's text, yet it is the only way to reach 'eleven ids' cited while only ten are classified (four passing: queued, retired, own, and the renamed file's declared `SA-0023`; six explicitly failing). The implementation's choice to exclude `README.md` from `spec_ids()` (mirroring `_retired_ids`'s own treatment, per the spec's 'How a spec file's id is read elsewhere' note) is internally consistent, but it makes the witness assert a different exact count than the acceptance criterion literally states, so the criterion as written is not met by this diff.
